subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Representativeness Heuristic
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Representativeness Heuristic.

hook.text: Linda is 31, outspoken, and studied philosophy. Is she more likely a bank teller—or a feminist bank teller?

buildup.text: Most people say feminist bank teller. But that's logically impossible—it's a subset of all bank tellers.

discovery.text: We judge probability by resemblance. Linda 'looks like' a feminist, so we ignore base rates entirely.

twist.text: Even statisticians fall for this. Narrative fit overrides mathematical logic in the human mind.

climax.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that we confuse 'sounds right' with 'is probable' across countless domains.

punchline.text: A good story beats good math—in your brain.

quiz.question: What is the conjunction fallacy?
options: Judging a specific combo as more likely than its parts
